meta.title: astrolol
meta.description: astrolol is a free, open-source, web-based platform for controlling your telescope, camera, mount and guiding from any browser.
meta.og_description: Free, open-source, web-based platform for controlling your telescope, camera, mount and guiding from any browser.

hero.lead: astrolol is a headless control platform for your imaging rig. It runs on a small Linux computer and you drive it from a laptop, tablet or phone on your network.

features.title: Everything at the scope, in one place.
features.lead: Device control, imaging, guiding and automation behind one event-driven backend, with a live view that stays in sync across every connected client.

cards.title: Device control
cards.body: astrolol remembers the devices (INDI or native) that are part of your profile and reconnects them automatically.

cards.title: Parallel imaging
cards.body: Astrolol supports taking pictures from many cameras at once, with synchronized dithering.

cards.title: Guiding & plate solving
cards.body: Guiding with PHD2 or the integrated guider module.

cards.title: Sequencer
cards.body: Queue a night's plan: target, slew, center, guide, dither, meridian flip and recover from the usual incidents.

cards.title: REST API
cards.body: Every feature is reachable over a documented REST and WebSocket API, not just the bundled UI — the only free, open-source telescope control platform built this way. Script it, or build your own client.

cards.title: Plugins
cards.body: astrolol is completely designed over a plugin architecture, making it easy to extend it and implement new features or drivers.

start.title: Three things, then you're imaging.

steps.title: Install it at the scope
steps.body: Runs on a Raspberry Pi or any small Linux box bolted to the mount. 1GiB RAM recommended.

steps.title: Connect your gear
steps.body: astrolol talks to INDI drivers out of the box, and has a native driver for Sky-Watcher EQMOD.

steps.title: Open a browser
steps.body: Open astrolol from a browser or from your phone.

start.install_note: Setup depends on your hardware and OS.
